messages:
maya (oncall): noticing spike in 5xx for prompt-router-new endpoint since the 11:20 deploy. Canary failing fast. logs show timeouts to the new proxy variant. :rotating_light:
ops-bot: incident detected: canary_errors > 5% over 2m for service=prompt-router-new (alert id: alert-9812). paging maya.
maya (oncall): I'm on it, looking at canary dashboard now. attaching snippet: ```curl -sS https://internal-monitoring/api/errors?svc=prompt-router-new | jq .rate``` shows 7.3% 5xx over last 1m.
ben (sre): joining. any obvious infra OOMs or kernel messages?
maya (oncall): not seeing OOMs. New endpoint proxies to experimental proxy pool; connections appear to be being reset by the proxy. stack traces show EOF during upstream read.
eli (infra): digging into the proxy nodes, one host in the canary pool has a high conn count. `ss -s` on node-enc-07 shows many TIME_WAIT but also a steady stream of RST. CPU and mem look normal.
sara (product): customers on stable route are ok? any visible user impact?
ben (sre): quick customer impact check: sample of traffic that hit the new endpoint shows ~3% of production requests returned 504 or closed stream; roughly 0.8% of total traffic. hitting a few /chat completions. recommend kill-switch flip for canary to route traffic back to stable.
maya (oncall): agreed. I'm going to flip the FF to force routing away from prompt-router-new.
maya (oncall): /ff toggle prompt-router-new false --env=prod  (issuing via ff-service)
ops-bot: feature-flag change queued: prompt-router-new -> OFF (requested by maya). id=chg-20260315-11:33
ben (sre): confirming state change with `/ff status prompt-router-new`
maya (oncall): confirmed: prompt-router-new == OFF across all regions.
ops-bot: rollout daemon: re-route policy applied, migrating 100% of traffic from prompt-router-new -> prompt-router-stable over ~30s.
matt (secondary): taking pager from maya in 10m; ping me if anything else pops.
eli (infra): observing connection error rate drop on node-enc-07 after flip. latency trending back to baseline.
ben (sre): canary error rate back down to 0.5% within 90s. looks like kill-switch worked.
sara (product): any customers we should proactively notify? I can draft a note. Impact was small but affected completions.
ben (sre): quick postmortem checklist: 1) root cause triage on why proxy reset under canary, 2) revert commit or scale proxy pool, 3) test harness for the proxy's new conn handling, 4) ensure canary thresholds cause automated FF rollback next time.
maya (oncall): creating incident ticket and assigning to eli+ben for detailed RCA. ticket: INC-20260315-84 created.
ops-bot: Incident INC-20260315-84 created by maya (oncall). Severity: P2.
matt (secondary): I've picked up pager. will be oncall until 18:00 UTC.
eli (infra): quick note — there was a rare TCP keepalive handling difference in the new proxy build; initial hypothesis: ephemeral port exhaustion combined with a proxy bug causing upstream resets under load patterns we didn't emulate in canary. I'll capture kernel netstat dumps and the proxy config.
ben (sre): plan: rollback proxy build from canary tag -> previous stable tag on canary pool and re-run canary with synthetic load. I'll coordinate the rollback tomorrow during low-traffic window unless product escalates.
sara (product): i'll prepare a customer-facing blurb: short note + timeline + remediation steps. no formal outage declared since overall service remained up, but we'll mention partial degraded responses for small subset.
maya (oncall): closing thread: default route restored, FF flipped, canary metrics normalized. Folks: if you need anything else tag me. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: incident INC-20260315-84 status -> monitoring. last action: FF toggle by maya at 2026-03-15T11:33:48Z.
